counterexamples.evidence: L5 renders only “You had a forced win — it resolves deep, via a parity battle via a parity line completing at column 6. Column 6 was the move that kept it; the played move let the opponent deny it at column 7.” The assembled prompt (assembleGroundedPrompt) contains no obligation to explain the parity reason, so all 3/3 runs restate the outcome. The real cause is board-visible: on the decision board (movestring 32) the ascending diagonal c4r1-c5r2-c6r3-c7r4 already holds P1’s move-1 disc at c4r1 and its remaining empties are all even-parity (zcount 2/2/4), and playing column 6 (bestCol 5, solver score +2 vs 0 for the played column 2) is what wins the race to c6r3.

Runs 0 and 1 use line words but emit no line handle, the exact shape mismatch the prompt’s own “MATCH THE SHAPE OF YOUR WORDS” block warns against; run 1 emits zero zone tags. The handle was offered and required in the assembled prompt, so this is model-side, not information suppression.
